name: Blue cheese (generic)
definition: blue-veined cheese sold as blue cheese or under a variety name with no kind of its own (Danish blue, Cambozola); not the Gorgonzola, Stilton or Roquefort types.
reason: Rule P(1): sold generically by unrelated makers; the blue leaf held only two protected types, so plain and minor blues had no home.

name: Blue cheese (Roquefort)
definition: blue-veined sheep's-milk cheese of the Roquefort type, cave-ripened, moist and crumbly.
reason: Rule P(3) names Roquefort: protected, no generic sibling sold under its name; kind level provisional until two-region sellers attested (C11).

name: Dairy coffee creamer
definition: milk- or cream-based liquid or powder made to whiten coffee or tea, often sweetened or flavoured; plain cream goes by its fat tier.
reason: R-96 gap; memo 9.7 and K-49 keep creamers J3; retailer sells dairy creamers as a type, mirroring plant creamer J3.7.4.02.

name: Clotted cream
definition: cream heated and slowly cooled until a thick crusted layer of fat forms, spooned rather than poured, of the highest cream fat tier.
reason: Cooked cream that neither pours nor whips, sold under its own name; double cream's definition excludes it; process makes a different product (JC4).

name: Single (light) cream
reason: Heat-stable cooking use on cream of a stated fat tier; the fat tier decides single (J3.2.1.01) or whipping (J3.2.1.02), like barista.

name: Aerosol whipped cream
definition: cream, usually sweetened and stabilised, packed under propellant gas in a can that whips it as it is dispensed.
reason: Can whips it on dispensing and the recipe adds sugar and stabiliser: not the same product (JC4); sold as own category; sweetened stays J3 (J-7).

name: Ricotta
definition: whey cheese made by reheating whey, often with milk added, and lifting the fine curd; soft, moist and mild.
reason: Whey cheese sold generically by unrelated makers (Rule P(1)); key step 7 gives Fresh and whey cheeses, which had no whey-cheese kind.

name: Mascarpone
definition: soft, thick fresh cheese of cream set with acid, rich and mild.
reason: Acid-set cream cheese sold under its own name by unrelated makers (Rule P(1)); compared apart from cream cheese (milk and cream).

name: Halloumi
definition: semi-hard cheese kept in brine whose curd is heated in whey and folded; firm, squeaky and non-melting when grilled.
reason: Key step 5 (brine); form unlike feta's crumbly curd; a kind under P(1) or P(3) alike; Halloumi PDO becomes its named form.

name: Provolone
definition: stretched-curd cheese moulded in pear, sausage or cylinder shapes and aged, mild (dolce) to sharp (piccante).
reason: Pasta filata (key step 6) sold generically by unrelated makers (Rule P(1)); Provolone Valpadana PDO becomes a named form.

name: Edam
definition: semi-hard pressed round cheese of Dutch type, mild, often sold in a wax coat.
reason: Variety made by unrelated makers in many countries (Rule P(1)); firm by Codex (key step 9); Edam Holland PGI becomes a named form.

name: Gruyère
definition: hard Alpine cooked-pressed cheese with a brushed or smear rind and few or no holes, nutty, aged for months.
reason: Hard smear-rind cheese goes by firmness (tree precedence); variety under P(1) or P(3) alike; Le Gruyère AOP, Gruyère PGI become named forms.

name: Hard cooked-pressed cheese (Comté)
definition: hard cooked-pressed cheese of the Jura type, made in large wheels from raw cow's milk and aged for months.
reason: Tree precedence names Comté as a variety placed by firmness; buyers compare it with Gruyère; Rule P(3) kind, level provisional (C11).

name: Manchego
definition: firm pressed cheese with a basket-weave rind, of sheep's milk in Spain (cow's or mixed milk in Mexican manchego), sold fresh to aged.
reason: Variety sold under the name by unrelated makers (Rule P(1)); firm in its ordinary retail form (key step 9); Queso Manchego PDO a named form.

name: Spreadable soft cheese
reason: Names the milk species, an attribute in Cheese (tree precedence); a fresh goat log is spreadable soft cheese; aged goat cheeses go by variety.

name: Soured milk (mesophilic cultured milk)
definition: milk fermented whole by a mesophilic lactic culture at room temperature, mild, thick or ropy, poured or spooned; not buttermilk (filmjölk, viili, piimä).
reason: Culture-defined type outside yoghurt, kefir and kumys cultures (sub-family axis); no kind covers it; tested after kumys. Needs a seller page.

name: Filmjölk
reason: Swedish regional name of mesophilic soured milk (C11): non-maker named form under the new generic kind, Nordic tradition tag.

name: Viili
reason: Finnish ropy mesophilic soured milk: regional name under the new generic kind (C11), Nordic tradition tag.

name: Matzoon
reason: Already non-maker named form NF-J3.3.01-004 under yoghurt; its warm yoghurt-type culture keeps it there; no change.
